title: “‘The world is deficient, longing, a slave to craving’ — that, great king, is the fourth exposition of the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One,…
content: “‘The world is deficient, longing, a slave to craving’ — that, great king, is the fourth exposition of the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Having known, seen, and heard that exposition, I went forth from the household life into homelessness.”

title: “Monks, what is a course of practice that is painful in the present but yields pleasant results in the future? Here, monks, a person by…
content: “Monks, what is a course of practice that is painful in the present but yields pleasant results in the future? Here, monks, a person by nature has strong lust, and he constantly experiences painful and grievous feelings born of lust. By nature he has strong ill-will, and constantly experiences painful and grievous feelings born of ill-will. By nature he has strong delusion, and constantly experiences painful and grievous feelings born of delusion. With pain and grief, with tearful face and crying, he lives the holy life that is fully complete and pure. At the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world, in this realm. This, monks, is called a course of practice that is painful in the present but yields pleasant results in the future.”

title: - “Venerable sir, I do not understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One regarding the purpose of purity of virtue.” - “Monk, if you…
content: - “Venerable sir, I do not understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One regarding the purpose of purity of virtue.” - “Monk, if you do not understand the Dhamma I have taught regarding the purpose of purity of virtue, then how, monk, do you understand the Dhamma I have taught?” - “Venerable sir, I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One as greed and the removal of greed.” - “Good, good, monk! Good, monk! You understand the Dhamma taught by me as greed and the removal of greed. It is for the purpose of greed and the removal of greed, monk, that the Dhamma is taught by me. What do you think, monk: Is the eye permanent or impermanent?” - “Impermanent, venerable sir.” - “The ear … The nose … The tongue … The body … Is the mind permanent or impermanent?” - “Impermanent, venerable sir.” - “What is impermanent — is that suffering or happiness?” - “Suffering, venerable sir.” - “What is impermanent, suffering, subject to change — is it fitting to regard it as: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” - “No, venerable sir.” - “Seeing thus, a well-taught noble disciple becomes disenchanted with the eye … disenchanted with the mind … Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate … He knows: ‘… there is no more of this state of being.’”

title: “And what, monks, is dwelling heedfully? If one lives without restraint of the eye faculty, monks, his mind is defiled by forms cognizable by the…
content: “And what, monks, is dwelling heedfully? If one lives without restraint of the eye faculty, monks, his mind is defiled by forms cognizable by the eye. For one with a defiled mind, there is no gladness. Without gladness, there is no rapture. Without rapture, there is no tranquility. Without tranquility, suffering remains. For one who is suffering, the mind does not become concentrated. When the mind is not concentrated, phenomena are not clearly seen. When phenomena are not clearly seen, he is called ‘one who dwells heedfully’ … the ear faculty … the nose faculty … the tongue faculty … the body faculty … If one lives without restraint of the mind faculty, his mind is defiled by phenomena cognizable by the mind. For one with a defiled mind, there is no gladness … he is called ‘one who dwells heedfully.’ Thus, monks, is dwelling heedfully.”

title: “Householders, if those wanderers of other sects ask you: ‘By what basis, by what tradition, do you speak of those venerable ones as follows: Surely…
content: “Householders, if those wanderers of other sects ask you: ‘By what basis, by what tradition, do you speak of those venerable ones as follows: Surely those venerable ones are free from lust, or are on the path to subduing lust; free from ill-will, or on the path to subduing ill-will; free from delusion, or on the path to subduing delusion?’—when asked thus, householders, you should answer those wanderers of other sects: ‘Those venerable ones dwell in remote lodgings in isolated forests. But in such places there are no forms cognizable by the eye that they could see and then delight in; no sounds cognizable by the ear … no odors cognizable by the nose … no tastes cognizable by the tongue … no tangibles cognizable by the body that they could feel and then delight in. Good sirs, by this basis, by this tradition, we speak of those venerable ones as follows: Surely those venerable ones are free from lust, or are on the path to subduing lust; free from ill-will … free from delusion, or on the path to subduing delusion.’”

title: “Good sirs, what is the pursuit of the past? ‘My eye in the past was such and such, forms were such and such, and consciousness…
content: “Good sirs, what is the pursuit of the past? ‘My eye in the past was such and such, forms were such and such, and consciousness there was bound by desire and lust. Because consciousness is bound by desire and lust, he delights in that. Delighting in that, he pursues the past. My ear in the past … nose … tongue … body … mind in the past was such and such, phenomena were such and such, and consciousness there was bound by desire and lust. Because consciousness is bound by desire and lust, he delights in that. Delighting in that, he pursues the past.’ This, good sirs, is the pursuit of the past.”

title: Elder Nisabha: Having abandoned the five strands of sensual pleasure, Those things so agreeable, Which delight the mind — With faith, I went forth, Putting…
content:
Elder Nisabha:

Having abandoned the five strands of sensual pleasure,
Those things so agreeable,
Which delight the mind —
With faith, I went forth,
Putting an end to suffering.

I do not delight in death,
I do not delight in life.
I await the time,
Mindful and clearly comprehending.

title: “Monks, before my enlightenment, while I was still a bodhisatta, not yet fully enlightened, I thought: ‘The five strands of sensual pleasure that this mind…
content: “Monks, before my enlightenment, while I was still a bodhisatta, not yet fully enlightened, I thought: ‘The five strands of sensual pleasure that this mind formerly experienced — now past, ceased, changed — regarding them, my mind becomes inflamed when they are present, and diminishes when they are future, not yet attained.’ Then, monks, I thought: ‘The five strands of sensual pleasure that this mind formerly experienced — now past, ceased, changed — regarding them, for my own benefit, I will dwell heedful, protecting my mind with mindfulness.’ Therefore, monks, regarding the five strands of sensual pleasure that your minds formerly experienced — now past, ceased, changed — your minds become inflamed when they are present, and diminish when they are future, not yet attained. Therefore, monks, regarding the five strands of sensual pleasure that your minds formerly experienced — now past, ceased, changed — for your own benefit, dwell heedful, protecting your minds with mindfulness.”

title: “Monks, whatever is impermanent, you should abandon your desire for it. And what, monks, is impermanent? Form, monks, is impermanent … Feeling … Perception ……
content: “Monks, whatever is impermanent, you should abandon your desire for it. And what, monks, is impermanent? Form, monks, is impermanent … Feeling … Perception … Formations … Consciousness is impermanent — there you should abandon your desire. Whatever is impermanent, monks, there you should abandon your desire.”

title: Māra: You are young and beautiful, I am young and in my prime. With the five-tuned lute, Enjoy yourself, Khemā. Elder Nun Khemā: With this…
content:
Māra:

You are young and beautiful,
I am young and in my prime.
With the five-tuned lute,
Enjoy yourself, Khemā.

Elder Nun Khemā:

With this foul body,
Diseased and fragile —
I am disenchanted, disgusted.
Sensual desire has been uprooted.

Sensual desires are like swords and spears —
The aggregates are a chopping block.
What you call sensual pleasure —
I have now abandoned it.

Everywhere, delight is destroyed,
The mass of delusion is shattered.
Know this, O Evil One —
You are defeated, Māra.

You worship the stars!
You worship fire in the deep forest —
You do not know the truth —
Fools think it is pure.

But I pay homage
To the Awakened One, the Supreme Man,
Who has escaped all suffering,
Following the Teacher’s instruction.
